intervention: Root-purpose provenance across multi-agent handoffs
operative_instrument_legal_basis: Agent protocol, audit standard, procurement clause
implementer: Agent providers, deployers, auditors, public procurers
legal_scope_correction: Research proposal
mechanism_targeted: Bind every delegated subtask, tool call, generated artifact, and terminal action to a signed root-purpose record, with explicit scope changes and controller identity.
causal_chain_point: Capability → controller → delegated vector
expected_effect: Makes harmful composition inspectable and prevents local compliance from substituting for end-to-end purpose review.
main_failure_evasion: False or vague root purposes; off-ledger work; laundering through external tools; excessive retention of sensitive prompts.
rights_trade_offs: Minimize retained content, separate oversight metadata from message content, and provide due process for contested classifications.

decision_rationale: Decision follows legal maturity, causal plausibility, reversibility and current evidence—not a composite score.

intervention: Machine-readable authorization boundaries and least privilege for agents

intervention: Official-source grounding for verifiable election-administration facts

intervention: Election-specific systemic-risk assessment and mitigation for very large platforms and search engines
operative_instrument_legal_basis: Digital Services Act Articles 34-35 plus Commission election guidelines
implementer: VLOPs and VLOSEs; supervised by the European Commission and Digital Services Coordinators
legal_scope_correction: In force; guidelines are the current compliance benchmark
mechanism_targeted: Require VLOPs and VLOSEs to assess election-specific risks from service design, ranking, advertising, generative AI, coordinated manipulation and local context; deploy mitigations before the electoral period, maintain an incident mechanism and publish a post-election review.
causal_chain_point: AI-enabled campaign or state actor → platform design and ranking → voter exposure and salience → belief, attention or trust change → agency transfer to campaign and platform → concentrated agenda-setting → electoral distortion.
agency_domain: Epistemic; Attentional; Evaluative; Decisional; Relational; Collective / institutional

decision_rationale: Enforce legal scope; measure implementation and rights costs separately from legal existence.

intervention: Recommender-system transparency for online platforms
operative_instrument_legal_basis: Digital Services Act Articles 27 and 38
implementer: Online platforms and VLOPs; enforced by Digital Services Coordinators and the European Commission
legal_scope_correction: DSA Article 27 recommender transparency for online platforms; the Article 38 non-profiling option is separated into I-084.
mechanism_targeted: Disclose in clear language the main recommender parameters and users' options to modify or influence them under DSA Article 27. The non-profiling option is coded separately under I-084.
causal_chain_point: Platform optimisation → personalised feed → repeated political exposure → attention and preference shaping → agency transfer to platform → concentrated control of the decision environment.
expected_effect: Creates an exit from inferred-vulnerability targeting and gives users some control over how political attention is allocated.
main_failure_evasion: Non-profiled does not mean neutral or safe; platforms can nudge users toward the default; transparency may be too abstract; chronological feeds can still be gamed by coordinated networks.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Default versus alternative feed prominence; opt-in and persistence rates; political-content concentration and source diversity; exposure inequality; user comprehension; differential manipulation prevalence by feed mode.
decision_rationale: Enforce legal scope; measure implementation and rights costs separately from legal existence.

intervention: Ban on manipulative interface design and dark patterns
operative_instrument_legal_basis: Digital Services Act Article 25
implementer: Online platforms; national Digital Services Coordinators
legal_scope_correction: In force

causal_chain_point: Platform or campaign-controlled interface → deceptive choice architecture → reduced reflection or coerced disclosure → behavioural or dependency change → agency transfer → platform power concentration.
expected_effect: Targets the decision environment itself rather than only false content, making it directly relevant to agency transfer.
main_failure_evasion: Boundary between persuasion and manipulation is context-sensitive; enforcement may focus on commercial UX and miss political onboarding, consent flows, notification pressure or agent defaults.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.

decision_rationale: Enforce legal scope; measure implementation and rights costs separately from legal existence.

intervention: Machine-readable marking of AI-generated content and visible deepfake disclosure

intervention: Time-bound election Rapid Response System for platform escalation
operative_instrument_legal_basis: Code of Conduct on Disinformation election cooperation and Rapid Response System
implementer: EDMO, fact-checkers, civil society signatories and participating platforms
legal_scope_correction: Operational since the 2024 European Parliament election and reused in later elections
mechanism_targeted: Allow authorised non-platform signatories, fact-checkers and civil society to rapidly flag severe, time-sensitive content, accounts or trends and discuss response with platforms under their policies.
causal_chain_point: Late-breaking synthetic or coordinated incident → rapid spread → no time for ordinary review → belief, turnout or legitimacy shock → temporary agency transfer; an escalation lane compresses response time.
expected_effect: Creates a trusted, fast channel for the final hours when ordinary notice systems are too slow.
main_failure_evasion: Platform policy still controls action; privileged flaggers may miss local or minority-language incidents; false positives and government pressure can chill speech; no common service-level obligation.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Acknowledgement and disposition time; reach accrued before action; escalation acceptance rate; false-positive and appeal outcomes; coverage by country, language, platform and modality.
decision_rationale: Decision follows legal maturity, causal plausibility, reversibility and current evidence—not a composite score.

intervention: European Centre for Democratic Resilience and reinforced election coordination
operative_instrument_legal_basis: European Democracy Shield institutional mechanism
implementer: European Commission, participating Member States, candidate countries, EU bodies and stakeholder platform

legal_scope_correction: Launched 2026-02-24; operational design still maturing
mechanism_targeted: Pool Member State, EU and civil-society expertise to anticipate, detect and respond to FIMI and disinformation; connect election networks, DSA data access, political-ad data and operational response.
causal_chain_point: Cross-border actor → fragmented national signals → delayed attribution and response → accumulating trust and agenda effects → agency transfer to hostile actor; pooled awareness reverses the asymmetry.
expected_effect: Addresses cross-platform and cross-border coordination gaps and can turn dispersed signals into a common operational picture.
main_failure_evasion: Mandate overlap, politicised attribution, intelligence-to-public-evidence gaps, centralisation without accountability and slow information sharing.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Shared alerts and lead time; Member State participation; joint analyses; cross-platform incident resolution; public attribution quality; exercise and after-action improvements.
decision_rationale: Decision follows legal maturity, causal plausibility, reversibility and current evidence—not a composite score.
family_name: European Centre for Democratic Resilience and reinforced election coordination

intervention: Mandatory digital imprints on paid political material and specified organic campaign material
operative_instrument_legal_basis: Elections Act 2022 Part 6 and Electoral Commission statutory guidance
implementer: Campaigners, candidates, parties, police and Electoral Commission
legal_scope_correction: In force since November 2023; guidance updated in 2026
mechanism_targeted: Require covered digital material, including social posts, online ads, podcasts and publicly distributed messaging-app content, to state who promoted and on whose behalf it was published.
causal_chain_point: Campaign or third party → unattributed digital communication → voter → mistaken source trust → agency transfer to hidden promoter → opaque political power.
expected_effect: Preserves contestability by letting voters and regulators identify the responsible campaign actor.
main_failure_evasion: Organic material by unregistered actors has gaps; private messages and cross-border actors are hard to enforce; an imprint does not disclose targeting, spend, AI use or beneficial funder.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.

family_name: Mandatory digital imprints on paid political material and specified organic campaign material

intervention: Systemic platform duties for criminal foreign-interference content
operative_instrument_legal_basis: National Security Act 2023 plus Online Safety Act 2023
implementer: Online services and Ofcom, with police and national-security bodies
legal_scope_correction: Illegal-content duties in force from 2025-03-17
mechanism_targeted: Treat the National Security Act foreign-interference offence as a priority offence, requiring in-scope services to assess risk, prevent users encountering illegal material and minimise its availability; Ofcom can impose major fines and disruption measures.
causal_chain_point: Foreign power or proxy → covert online conduct → UK voters and institutions → trust, behaviour or legitimacy change → agency transfer abroad → democratic harm.
expected_effect: Creates a systemic duty to act on covert hostile-state operations rather than relying only on voluntary moderation.
main_failure_evasion: Most domestic misinformation and lawful manipulative persuasion remain outside scope; attribution to a foreign power is difficult; encryption and cross-border evidence constrain action; overreach risks political surveillance.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Foreign-interference risk assessments; detected networks; time-to-disruption; Ofcom enforcement; successful prosecutions; reach before removal; false attribution and appeal outcomes.
decision_rationale: Enforce legal scope; measure implementation and rights costs separately from legal existence.
family_name: Systemic platform duties for criminal foreign-interference content

intervention: Election-authority deepfake detection and impact-monitoring pilot
operative_instrument_legal_basis: Electoral Commission operational pilot with the Home Office Accelerated Capability Environment
implementer: UK Electoral Commission and ACE, with parties, candidates, platforms and police
legal_scope_correction: Pilot ran around the May 2026 elections; full findings due autumn 2026
mechanism_targeted: Monitor online audio and video for false candidate depictions or election-process claims, track reach, coordinate corrections or requested takedowns, and refer serious content to police or other bodies.
causal_chain_point: AI generator → candidate or authority impersonation → voter → false belief or suppressed participation → agency transfer to fabricator; detection and authoritative correction interrupt spread.
expected_effect: Gives the election authority an early-warning picture and a route to authenticate candidate or process claims.
main_failure_evasion: Detectors are brittle and can generate false positives; monitoring may miss closed messaging and low-resource languages; requests lack compulsory force; public alarms can amplify a fake.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Precision and recall against adjudicated samples; time-to-detection; reach before correction; candidate response time; correction penetration; referrals and platform outcomes.
decision_rationale: Decision follows legal maturity, causal plausibility, reversibility and current evidence—not a composite score.
family_name: Election-authority deepfake detection and impact-monitoring pilot

intervention: Statutory political-ad libraries and regulator/researcher access to platform exposure data
operative_instrument_legal_basis: Electoral Commission reform recommendation
implementer: Would require UK Parliament or government, platforms, Electoral Commission, Ofcom and ICO
legal_scope_correction: Proposed; not a general statutory requirement as of 2026-08-11
mechanism_targeted: Require every platform carrying political ads to maintain a comprehensive library with sponsor, targeting, actual reach and spend, and create meaningful data access for regulators and independent researchers.
causal_chain_point: Opaque platform ads and ranking → unobservable targeting and amplification → voter influence → agency transfer → no accountability; access makes the pathway measurable.
expected_effect: Would close the UK's reliance on voluntary, inconsistent libraries and make algorithmic political reach auditable.
main_failure_evasion: Privacy and trade-secret limits; platform exit from ads; organic influence remains hidden; data can arrive too late for election response.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Platform coverage; field completeness; API availability; actual versus reported reach; researcher access times; detected foreign or unlawful spending.
decision_rationale: Decision follows legal maturity, causal plausibility, reversibility and current evidence—not a composite score.

intervention: Treat AI-cloned voices in robocalls as artificial voices requiring consent
operative_instrument_legal_basis: FCC Declaratory Ruling under the TCPA
implementer: FCC, state attorneys general and telecom providers
legal_scope_correction: In force; applied in the New Hampshire robocall matter
mechanism_targeted: Apply TCPA consent and identification rules to AI-generated or cloned voices classified as artificial or prerecorded voices, subject to statutory exemptions.
causal_chain_point: Campaign operative → cloned candidate voice → mass calls → false instruction or turnout suppression → agency transfer to caller → electoral harm.
expected_effect: Uses mature robocall law to impose consent and enforcement costs on a high-risk impersonation vector.
main_failure_evasion: Caller-ID spoofing, offshore operators, peer-to-peer messages and non-voice synthetic content can evade; consent exceptions and enforcement latency remain.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Complaint volume; blocked calls; trace-back success; time-to-enforcement; penalties collected; repeat offending; estimated voter reach.
decision_rationale: Enforce legal scope; measure implementation and rights costs separately from legal existence.
notes: This is not a ban on every AI political message: prior express consent and exemptions depend on call purpose and context.

intervention: Apply federal fraudulent-misrepresentation rules to AI that falsely claims campaign authority
operative_instrument_legal_basis: FEC interpretive rule under 52 U.S.C. §30124 and 11 C.F.R. §110.16
implementer: Federal Election Commission
legal_scope_correction: Interpretive rule adopted; broader AI rulemaking declined in 2024
mechanism_targeted: Clarify that existing law can cover AI communications where a candidate or agent falsely purports to speak, act or fundraise on behalf of another candidate or party; it does not generally prohibit false depictions with a truthful disclaimer.
causal_chain_point: Candidate or agent → AI impersonation of rival campaign authority → voter or donor → source deception → agency transfer to impersonator → electoral or financial harm.
expected_effect: Protects authentic campaign authority and donations from a limited class of AI impersonation.
main_failure_evasion: Leaves most candidate deepfakes, lies, issue ads and third-party content outside the rule; FEC deadlock and slow enforcement reduce real-time value.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Complaints and matters under review; time to disposition; proven authority impersonations; voter or donor losses; repeat incidents.
decision_rationale: Decision follows legal maturity, causal plausibility, reversibility and current evidence—not a composite score.
notes: The FEC interpretation covers two narrow fraudulent-misrepresentation settings involving purported campaign authority; it is not a federal deepfake ban.

intervention: On-air and political-file disclosure of AI-generated content in broadcast political ads
operative_instrument_legal_basis: FCC Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, proceeding 24-211
implementer: Would be implemented by FCC-regulated broadcasters, cable and satellite entities
legal_scope_correction: Proposed in 2024; no final rule identified as of 2026-08-11
mechanism_targeted: Require radio and television political ads using AI-generated content to carry an on-air notice and a written disclosure in the station's political file.
causal_chain_point: Campaign → synthetic broadcast ad → mass audience → false authenticity belief → agency transfer to advertiser → electoral influence.
expected_effect: Would make synthetic content visible in legacy mass media and create an inspectable record.
main_failure_evasion: FCC jurisdiction largely excludes online and streaming ads; broad definitions may over-label routine editing; disclosure may not neutralise deception.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: If adopted: disclosure compliance, political-file completeness, audience comprehension, complaints and cross-channel coverage gaps.
decision_rationale: Decision follows legal maturity, causal plausibility, reversibility and current evidence—not a composite score.
notes: The NPRM concerns radio and television political ads and political-file disclosure; it is not a final rule or a cross-platform online standard.

intervention: Platform duty to remove or label materially deceptive election deepfakes during a defined election window
operative_instrument_legal_basis: California Defending Democracy from Deepfake Deception Act, AB 2655
implementer: Large platforms and California enforcement authorities
legal_scope_correction: California AB 2655 was enacted but permanently enjoined as applied to the successful plaintiffs; appeal remained pending in 2026.
mechanism_targeted: California AB 2655 required large platforms to block specified deceptive election content or label it, provide reporting channels and respond within short timeframes.
causal_chain_point: AI creator → viral candidate or election deepfake → voter → false belief → agency transfer to creator → electoral harm; platform action attempts to stop distribution.
expected_effect: The intended effect was rapid reduction of deceptive synthetic reach; the actual contribution is a warning that broad platform-liability designs can collapse under intermediary-liability and speech law.
main_failure_evasion: Over-removal of satire and political speech, vague deception thresholds, prior-restraint concerns, Section 230 pre-emption and strategic reporting abuse.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: If redesigned: adjudicated precision, removal latency, restored-content rate, satire/parody false positives, reach prevented, litigation survival.
decision_rationale: Decision follows legal maturity, causal plausibility, reversibility and current evidence—not a composite score.

intervention: End-to-end cryptographic provenance and interoperable Content Credentials
operative_instrument_legal_basis: C2PA technical standard, complemented by NIST synthetic-content guidance
implementer: Model providers, camera and editing vendors, newsrooms, campaigns and platforms
legal_scope_correction: C2PA 2.2 published May 2025; adoption expanding but incomplete
mechanism_targeted: Bind signed assertions about origin and edit history to media, preserve or recover credentials across transformations, and display provenance at consumption.
causal_chain_point: Creator or model → media asset → platform and voter → uncertainty about source and edits → exploitable trust asymmetry; provenance restores verifiable history and contestability.
expected_effect: Authenticates known-good media and carries origin information across the supply chain, stronger than unreliable deepfake detection alone.
main_failure_evasion: Credential stripping, screenshots, unsigned legacy content, compromised signing keys, uneven adoption and the false inference that uncredentialed means fake.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Signing adoption by model, newsroom and campaign; credential survival across platforms; validation success; key compromise rate; user recognition; coverage of viral election media.
decision_rationale: Decision follows legal maturity, causal plausibility, reversibility and current evidence—not a composite score.

intervention: Election-specific human-rights risk assessment for digital platforms
operative_instrument_legal_basis: UNESCO Guidelines for the Governance of Digital Platforms
implementer: States, independent regulators and digital platforms
legal_scope_correction: Published and being used in implementation initiatives
mechanism_targeted: Require or encourage platforms to perform an election-cycle risk assessment, engage election administrators and civil society, assess design changes and take enhanced measures during elections and crises.
causal_chain_point: Platform product decision → altered amplification or access → electoral public → rights and agency effects → power concentration; assessment inserts rights review before deployment.
expected_effect: Offers a rights-based baseline for countries without a DSA-style regime and frames elections as a heightened-risk period.
main_failure_evasion: Soft-law compliance, regulator dependence, government capture and limited remedies; generic assessments may miss local languages, messaging apps and AI agents.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Publication and independence of assessments; stakeholder participation; mitigation closure; rights indicators; local-language coverage; post-election evaluation.
decision_rationale: Decision follows legal maturity, causal plausibility, reversibility and current evidence—not a composite score.

intervention: Political-party code for ethical digital campaigning and AI use
operative_instrument_legal_basis: International IDEA Code of Conduct for the 2024 European Parliament Elections
implementer: Political parties, with election bodies and civil-society monitoring
legal_scope_correction: Signed by European political parties in 2024; model available for national adaptation
mechanism_targeted: Secure public commitments by parties not to create, use or disseminate deceptive synthetic content or manipulative campaign techniques, to label AI use, protect cybersecurity and disclose campaign practices.
causal_chain_point: Party or campaign → AI-enabled content or targeting → electorate → preference or trust change → agency transfer to campaign → electoral advantage; party commitments constrain the controller directly.
expected_effect: Reaches party behaviour that platform rules cannot fully observe and establishes a public norm against agency-undermining tactics.
main_failure_evasion: No enforcement, selective sign-up, third-party proxies, vague AI definitions and incentives to defect in close races.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Party coverage; disclosed AI uses; independently verified violations; corrective action; proxy spending; voter awareness of commitments.
decision_rationale: Decision follows legal maturity, causal plausibility, reversibility and current evidence—not a composite score.

intervention: Forwarding limits and forwarded-message friction in encrypted messaging
operative_instrument_legal_basis: WhatsApp product policy and rate limits
implementer: WhatsApp/Meta
legal_scope_correction: Operational
mechanism_targeted: Limit forwarding to five chats and restrict already or highly forwarded messages to one chat at a time, while attaching forwarded labels.
causal_chain_point: Campaign network → encrypted mass forwarding → trusted peer groups → belief and mobilisation change → agency transfer to network organiser → concentrated hidden reach.
expected_effect: Adds cost and time to viral distribution without breaking end-to-end encryption or reading message content.
main_failure_evasion: Automation, many accounts, broadcast lists, groups, paid senders and copy-paste evade forwarding limits; legitimate civic information is also slowed; metadata enforcement can raise privacy concerns.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Reproduction number and diffusion depth; time to reach thresholds; highly-forwarded share; coordinated sender clusters; user reports; false and true content reach differential.
decision_rationale: Low-regret component with bounded evidence; monitor transfer and rights costs.

intervention: Technique-based prebunking and election media literacy
operative_instrument_legal_basis: Public information campaign, curriculum or platform-delivered inoculation videos
implementer: Election authorities, educators, media, civil society and platforms
jurisdiction: Global; adapted in EU election campaigns
legal_scope_correction: Field-tested and deployed; not universally institutionalised
mechanism_targeted: Expose voters in advance to short examples of manipulation techniques such as emotional manipulation, false dichotomies, scapegoating, incoherence and impersonation so they recognise tactics before encountering campaign content.
causal_chain_point: Manipulative content → voter cognitive vulnerability → belief or sharing change → agency transfer to persuader; prebunking strengthens reflective recognition before exposure.
expected_effect: Targets manipulation mechanisms rather than partisan truth adjudication and therefore better preserves pluralism and reflective agency.
main_failure_evasion: Effects decay, short clips may not transfer to novel AI tactics, motivated reasoning persists, blanket scepticism can erode trust, and campaigns may not reach the most exposed groups.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Pre-registered discernment and sharing outcomes; retention at 1, 4 and 12 weeks; exposure and completion; heterogeneous effects; trust calibration; actual sharing behaviour.
decision_rationale: Low-regret component with bounded evidence; monitor transfer and rights costs.
family_name: Technique-based prebunking and election media literacy

intervention: Platform political-ad authorisation, archive, AI disclosure and final-week ad freeze
operative_instrument_legal_basis: Meta advertising policies and election procedures
implementer: Meta
jurisdiction: Global disclosure policy with election-specific variations; final-week freeze used in the United States
legal_scope_correction: Operational for 2026 US midterms; EU political ads discontinued by Meta in October 2025
mechanism_targeted: Verify political advertisers, archive ads, require self-disclosure for realistic AI-created or altered political ads, add labels and bar new US political ads during the final week when rebuttal time is short.
causal_chain_point: Advertiser → paid microtargeted synthetic ad → selected voter → deceptive belief with little rebuttal time → agency transfer to advertiser and platform → electoral harm.
expected_effect: Raises source accountability and reduces last-minute paid deception on Meta services.
main_failure_evasion: Self-disclosure under-detection; old ads can continue during the freeze; organic posts, influencers and messaging remain; platform can change policy unilaterally; EU exit displaces rather than resolves influence.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Advertiser-verification failures; AI disclosure recall and classifier catch rate; ad-library completeness; rejected final-week ads; reach shifted to organic or off-platform channels.
decision_rationale: Decision follows legal maturity, causal plausibility, reversibility and current evidence—not a composite score.

intervention: Explicit, prominent and accessible disclosure of synthetic election content and the technology used
operative_instrument_legal_basis: TSE Resolution 23.610/2019 Article 9-B as amended by Resolutions 23.732/2024 and 23.755/2026
implementer: Candidates, parties, federations, coalitions and internet platforms; enforced by Electoral Justice
legal_scope_correction: Binding for the 2026 general election; campaign starts 2026-08-16
mechanism_targeted: Require election propaganda containing significantly AI-generated or altered text, audio, image or video to disclose fabrication or manipulation in a modality-specific form, including audio notices, watermark and audio description.
causal_chain_point: Campaign or supporter → synthetic political content → voter → mistaken authenticity → belief or preference change → agency transfer to content controller → electoral advantage.
expected_effect: Preserves source awareness without banning benign uses of AI and creates a clear enforcement hook.
main_failure_evasion: Manual non-compliance, re-uploads without labels, ambiguous significant alteration, disclosure fatigue and confusion between AI use and harmful manipulation.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Disclosure compliance by modality; label persistence; voter comprehension; removal and fine counts; false-positive exemptions; reach before correction.
decision_rationale: Enforce legal scope; measure implementation and rights costs separately from legal existence.

intervention: Ban on electoral deepfakes used to favour or harm a candidacy
operative_instrument_legal_basis: TSE Resolution 23.610 Article 9-C
implementer: Campaigns, Electoral Public Prosecutor, Electoral Justice and platforms
legal_scope_correction: In force for 2026
mechanism_targeted: Prohibit synthetic audio or video that creates, substitutes or alters the image or voice of a real, deceased or fictional person to favour or harm a candidacy, even with authorisation; violations can constitute abuse of power and misuse of media.
causal_chain_point: Campaign or proxy → deepfake → electorate → false candidate belief or reputational shock → agency transfer to fabricator → distorted electoral choice.
expected_effect: Directly targets candidate impersonation with consequences stronger than a label.
main_failure_evasion: Definition and satire boundaries, strategic litigation, over-removal, slow adjudication relative to virality and migration to anonymous foreign accounts.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Detected and adjudicated deepfakes; time-to-order and removal; reach; sanction consistency; appeal reversals; satire or news false positives.
decision_rationale: Enforce legal scope; measure implementation and rights costs separately from legal existence.

intervention: Ban on chatbots or avatars simulating conversation with a candidate or real person
operative_instrument_legal_basis: TSE Resolution 23.610 Article 9-B paragraph 3
implementer: Campaigns, parties, AI-service providers and Electoral Justice
legal_scope_correction: In force for 2026
mechanism_targeted: Permit campaign chatbots, avatars and synthetic intermediaries only with disclosure and prohibit simulation of direct interlocution with a candidate or another real person.
causal_chain_point: Campaign-controlled agent → simulated candidate intimacy → voter → trust, dependency or preference change → agency transfer to campaign → concentrated relational influence.
expected_effect: Prevents campaigns from manufacturing false personal relationships or apparent direct candidate commitments at scale.
main_failure_evasion: Bots can imply intimacy without literal impersonation; weak disclosure in long conversations; foreign tools and private messaging are hard to observe; overly broad enforcement could block accessibility uses.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Bot registration and disclosure compliance; impersonation test pass rate; conversation-level label persistence; complaints; voter source comprehension; private-channel coverage.
decision_rationale: Enforce legal scope; measure implementation and rights costs separately from legal existence.
family_name: Ban on chatbots or avatars simulating conversation with a candidate or real person

intervention: 72-hour pre-vote and 24-hour post-vote blackout for new synthetic candidate or public-figure content
operative_instrument_legal_basis: TSE Resolution 23.610 Article 9-B paragraph 3-A, added by Resolution 23.755/2026
implementer: Publishers, users, campaigns, platforms and Electoral Justice
legal_scope_correction: New and binding for the 4 October 2026 first round and possible 25 October second round
mechanism_targeted: Prohibit publication, republication and paid boosting of new AI-generated or altered content using a candidate's or public figure's image, voice or manifestation during the defined window, even if labelled.
causal_chain_point: Late synthetic release → high-velocity platforms → voters with no rebuttal time → belief or turnout shock → temporary agency capture → electoral or legitimacy harm.
expected_effect: Creates a quiet period for the exact late-breaker mechanism seen in Slovakia, Ireland and Buenos Aires.
main_failure_evasion: Very broad restraint on lawful speech, satire and journalism; re-publication detection at scale is difficult; adversaries can release just before the window or through foreign and encrypted channels.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Window violations; time-to-removal; reach accrued; pre-window displacement; appeal and restoration rate; impact on legitimate political media; cross-platform evasion.
decision_rationale: Enforce legal scope; measure implementation and rights costs separately from legal existence.

intervention: Electoral anti-favoritism rule for covered AI systems
operative_instrument_legal_basis: TSE Resolution 23.610 Article 28 paragraph 1-C, added by Resolution 23.755/2026
implementer: Providers of internet applications offering AI systems; Electoral Justice
legal_scope_correction: Brazilian electoral anti-favoritism rule for covered AI systems; not comprehensive neutrality.
mechanism_targeted: Prohibit covered AI systems from ranking, recommending or prioritizing electoral actors, expressing electoral preference, recommending a vote, or directly or indirectly favoring or disfavoring them.
causal_chain_point: AI provider or model controller → assistant answer or ranking → voter delegation and trust → voting preference or decision → agency transfer to AI controller → extreme concentration of electoral influence.
agency_domain: Attentional; Evaluative; Decisional; Relational; Collective / institutional
expected_effect: Directly targets agency transfer through assistants and recommendation, going beyond content labels and ad transparency.
main_failure_evasion: Overbroad neutrality can suppress legitimate comparative information; hidden bias can persist without explicit recommendations; defining indirect favour is difficult; foreign and open-source assistants may be unreachable.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Pre-registered multilingual neutrality audits; recommendation and refusal rates by candidate and issue; ranking parity; source diversity; correction latency; enforcement and appeal outcomes.
decision_rationale: Enforce legal scope; measure implementation and rights costs separately from legal existence.

intervention: Platform election-impact assessments, recommender-system mitigation and result transparency
operative_instrument_legal_basis: TSE Resolution 23.610 Article 9-D
implementer: Internet application providers; supervised by TSE and electoral courts
legal_scope_correction: In force for 2026
mechanism_targeted: Require platforms carrying political-electoral content to publish and implement measures against demonstrably false or severely decontextualised election content, improve recommendation systems, report results and conduct an election-year impact assessment including gendered political violence.
causal_chain_point: Platform ranking and monetisation → amplified manipulative content → voters and candidates → attention, trust and participation effects → agency transfer to platform and network controllers → democratic harm.
agency_domain: Epistemic; Attentional; Evaluative; Decisional; Relational; Collective / institutional
expected_effect: Shifts responsibility from notice-and-takedown to the platform's recommendation and product architecture.
main_failure_evasion: Platforms define their own assessment methods; ambiguous falsity thresholds; no guaranteed researcher access to exposure data; over-removal and political bias claims; small platforms may lack capacity.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Prevalence and recommendation-driven reach; risk coverage; mitigation effect sizes; gendered-harassment exposure; transparency-field completeness; independent replication; residual risk after each round.
decision_rationale: Enforce legal scope; measure implementation and rights costs separately from legal existence.

intervention: Immediate de-amplification, evidence preservation and narrowly bounded corrective promotion
operative_instrument_legal_basis: TSE Resolution 23.610 Article 9-D paragraphs 2-4
implementer: Platforms and Electoral Justice
legal_scope_correction: Narrow corrective-promotion remedy for irregularly boosted notably false or gravely decontextualized content.
mechanism_targeted: Require covered platforms to stop unlawful boosting or access, investigate involved accounts and preserve evidence; a same-form-and-reach corrective order is limited to false or severely decontextualised content that was irregularly boosted.
causal_chain_point: Manipulative incident → paid or algorithmic amplification → voter exposure → belief or trust change → agency transfer; de-amplification stops the vector and symmetric correction targets the affected audience.
agency_domain: Epistemic; Attentional; Evaluative; Decisional; Relational; Collective / institutional
expected_effect: Targets both distribution and residual false belief, and preserves evidence about coordinated accounts.
main_failure_evasion: Immediate action can over-remove lawful speech; matching original reach may amplify the falsehood; closed messaging lacks equivalent targeting; platforms may delete evidence before investigators access it.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Time from detection to de-amplification; reach prevented; evidence preservation; network recurrence; corrective reach overlap with exposed audience; belief correction and appeal outcomes.
decision_rationale: Enforce legal scope; measure implementation and rights costs separately from legal existence.
notes: Do not generalise the corrective remedy into a universal same-reach right; its statutory trigger and the prior irregular paid boost must be shown. Corrective promotion applies to irregularly boosted notably false or gravely decontextualized content; it does not guarantee equivalent organic reach.

intervention: Mandatory platform election-integrity compliance plans with measurable indicators
operative_instrument_legal_basis: TSE Resolution 23.755/2026 Article 125-B and Portaria 463/2026
implementer: Internet application providers and TSE presidency
legal_scope_correction: Ordinarily covers services above five million monthly active users in Brazil; plans due 2026-08-16, reports 2026-12-19.
mechanism_targeted: Require covered platforms to translate each electoral duty into concrete measures, baselines, measurable indicators, deadlines, expected results, impact assessment, evidence preservation, TSE channels and public/supervisory reporting.
causal_chain_point: Broad legal duties → vague platform promises → unmeasured safeguards → persistent agency transfer; measurable plans create ex ante accountability and enforcement hooks.
expected_effect: Can turn qualitative platform assurances into a comparable, time-bound control register before October.
main_failure_evasion: Indicators may measure activity rather than harm; plans may remain confidential; self-chosen baselines invite gaming; no explicit independent audit or researcher-access guarantee.

intervention: Pilot assistant loyalty and conflict audits before considering a statutory duty

implementer: Legislatures, consumer regulators and courts
legal_scope_correction: Pilot conflict and loyalty audits before considering a general statutory duty.

expected_effect: Changes the assistant's legal objective from engagement or platform value to user loyalty.
main_failure_evasion: Ambiguous best interests, paternalism, multiple principals, collective harms and enforcement difficulty.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Conflict incidence; user-benefit outcomes; privacy breaches; steering tests; remedies; autonomy and trust measures.
decision_rationale: Audit conflicts first; a general loyalty duty is premature and can become paternalistic.
notes: Duty must preserve reflective agency rather than permit paternalistic substitution of the provider's values.

intervention: Prohibit undisclosed sponsored steering and separate advice from platform commercial interests

expected_effect: Prevents the assistant's trusted interface from becoming invisible paid placement.
main_failure_evasion: Disclosure fatigue, indirect optimization, ecosystem self-preferencing and difficulty proving motive.
rights_trade_offs: Necessity, proportionality, privacy, speech, competition, and access require context-specific review.
metric: Undisclosed steering in audits; ranking changes by commercial relationship; disclosure comprehension; user choice divergence.
decision_rationale: Decision follows legal maturity, causal plausibility, reversibility and current evidence—not a composite score.
notes: Disclosure alone is insufficient where trust, personalization and provider power make consent non-meaningful.

intervention: Require scoped authorization, action ledgers, reversibility and renewal for agentic actions
operative_instrument_legal_basis: Agent conduct standard and product-safety requirement
implementer: AI regulators, sector regulators and standards bodies
legal_scope_correction: Policy proposal grounded in human-oversight and administrative-law precedents

intervention: Create an Agency Transfer Impact Assessment

legal_scope_correction: Prototype a six-axis Agency Transfer Profile; do not aggregate into a single score.

agency_domain: Epistemic; Attentional; Evaluative; Relational; Collective / institutional

intervention: Prototype freedom-of-thought safeguards for AI-mediated influence

intervention: Apply AI Act high-risk controls to systems intended to influence elections or voting behaviour
operative_instrument_legal_basis: EU AI Act Annex III 8(b) and Title III high-risk duties
implementer: Providers, deployers and market-surveillance authorities
legal_scope_correction: Annex III 8(b) is limited to intended electoral/voting influence with direct exposure; main duties apply 2027-12-02.
mechanism_targeted: Classify AI systems whose intended purpose is to influence an election or referendum outcome or voting behaviour as high-risk and apply lifecycle risk, documentation, logging, transparency, oversight, accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity duties when the timetable applies.
causal_chain_point: Provider or campaign → intended election-influence system → voter or electorate → belief, preference or voting-behaviour change → agency shifts to system controller → electoral influence concentrates.
expected_effect: Creates a direct lifecycle-control hook for AI intentionally designed to influence elections or voting behaviour.
main_failure_evasion: Intent-purpose avoidance, general-purpose assistant ambiguity, delayed application, self-assessment and offshore deployment.
rights_trade_offs: Constrain the category to intended election influence; protect administrative tools, lawful campaigning, satire, journalism, research, pluralism and appeal.
metric: Systems identified; conformity and deployer assessments; control closure; incidents; false inclusion/exclusion; complaints and appeals.
decision_rationale: Prepare implementation; do not code future duties as current effectiveness.
notes: Central omitted legal hook. It is not a general political-persuasion ban and does not validate an agency-transfer score.
